title: Frontline Learning Cards: Hazira gas release and fire, 2020
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document

bottom_line.text: A metering line went back into service after a gasket change without a test at design pressure.
The gas detectors showed an alarm on a panel but did not shut the plant down.

items.title: Test at design pressure before return to service
items.what_happened: After the gasket on the meter was replaced, the system was only pressurised to operating pressure and the meter went back online the next day [EVD-2894] [EVD-0185].
items.why_made_sense: There was no written procedure for calibrating these meters and taking them back into service, so a check at operating pressure looked like enough [EVD-2894].
items.organisation_changing: The committee pointed to a written return-to-service procedure that includes a test at design pressure before a high-pressure meter is put back in line [EVD-2894].
warning_signs: A seal or gasket that is not the original part
A return to service with no test record at design pressure
items.good_looks_like: No high-pressure meter goes back in line until the test at design pressure is recorded.
discussion: Where is the test record for a meter you put back in line?
Who can stop a return to service when the test is missing?

items.title: Know what the gas alarm does
items.what_happened: Hydrocarbon detectors were wired to an annunciator panel for display only, with no automatic shutdown or fire suppression [EVD-8657].
items.why_made_sense: An alarm on the panel looked like a working safeguard, and nothing on the panel said that it would not trip the plant [EVD-8657].
items.organisation_changing: The committee recommended interlocking the detection system to automatic plant shutdown and fire suppression [EVD-3452].
warning_signs: A gas alarm that only shows on a panel
No automatic action after a gas alarm
items.good_looks_like: Crews know which alarms trip equipment and which need a person to act at once.
